a.note: The most universal vowel. Stable across every major orthography.

b.note: Very widespread. Devoiced to /p/ by some Mandarin speakers.

d.note: Widespread. Merges toward /t/ for some Mandarin speakers.

e.note: Widespread, though quality drifts between /e/ and /ɛ/.

f.note: Absent from Korean and many Pacific and Australian languages.

g.note: Unstable across Arabic dialects (/g/, /dʒ/, /ɡ/ vary by region).

h.note: Silent for French, Italian and most Spanish readers.

i.note: One of the three quantal vowels; stable everywhere.

l.note: Widespread, but conflated with /r/ by Japanese and Korean speakers.

m.note: Present in essentially every spoken language.

n.note: Present in essentially every spoken language.

o.note: Widespread, though quality drifts between /o/ and /ɔ/.

p.note: Absent from Modern Standard Arabic; often realised as /b/.

r.note: Realised very differently by region: tap, trill, approximant, uvular.

s.note: Near-universal; a handful of Pacific languages lack it.

u.note: One of the three quantal vowels. French readers may say /y/.

v.note: Merges with /b/ for Spanish and Korean speakers.

z.note: Absent from Spanish (Peninsular) and Mandarin; merges with /s/.
